Introduction

With a sense of humble gratitude, we truly believe that the Family of Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate, was born not from a merely human plan, but by the initiative of God. It is a small part of the People of God which, moved by the Holy Spirit to respond to a free call from the Father, has gathered to work “in the Lord’s field”, collaborating in the Church and with the Church in the saving work of Christ (cf. Circular Letter, 1876).

For this reason, we recognize that the entire Charismatic Family is rooted in the inspiration of Blessed Mother Rosa Gattorno (cf. Memorie, p. 624), in whose heart vibrated the intuition regarding the various foundations, which would share a single spirit (Charism) and would all fully participate in all the spiritual merits of the Daughters of Saint Anne.

Animated by this urgent inner impulse, Mother Rosa repeatedly writes in her Memorie: “Remember the three drops of my blood that I showed you and shed on your heart; I told you that they would be the three Orders that you must [found]” (cf. Memorie, p. 665).

And coming to the year 1991, with the 18th General Chapter of the Daughters of Saint Anne, the long-awaited hour seems finally to have arrived for Blessed Anna Rosa Gattorno. The Institute, docile to the “breath of the Spirit”, embraces the “New Life”, recognizing its charism-inspired imprint.

From the writings of Mother Rosa

(Memorie, p. 261)

“A poor soul, so alone, with an abyss of matters to attend to, and also this which for me is the most dreadful thing that could exist: even the mere thought that I might do the slightest thing that is not His will…

Oh, how painful this is! I do not know how to describe it! To decide to let it go? Oh, how could I do that? What if I were mistaken?

And then I hear repeated within me:

— Remember the three drops of my blood that I showed you and that I poured upon your heart; I told you that they would be the three Orders that you must [found].

— Oh my Love, how can this be — I say within myself — I who am so old, how will I manage? I am full of sufferings, ill, and I feel that I can no longer go on. It is true that You make the dead live and the dying work, for I can say that my suffering is a daily agony; I do not speak of the pains, because it would take too long.”

With the invitation of the Second Vatican Council to “return to the sources”, the Sisters, Daughters of Saint Anne, having obtained permission from the Church to reopen the archives containing the writings of Mother Rosa — sealed due to her beatification process in Piacenza and Rome — found themselves faced with numerous documents in which they discovered an immense charismatic, spiritual, and historical richness. Meanwhile, the Spirit Himself was raising up, from North to South, from East to West, those whom He desired to be formed by this Charism.

From 1984, the Superior General at the time, Sr. A. Virginia Sinagra, listening to the desire of these individuals to share in the Institute’s spirituality—while living their own particular states of life and leaving space for the action of the Spirit - became increasingly attentive to any manifestation of this new vitality of the Charism, considering it a special initiative of God in the history of the Daughters of Saint Anne.

Considering also the numerical consistency of the requests, the validity of the proofs provided by the aspirants themselves and attested by the Sisters who had accompanied the emergence and development of spontaneous groups, as well as the positive judgment of the Provincial Superiors and the letters of numerous Bishops, the Mother deemed it appropriate to inform the Sisters gathered in Chapter about the reality of these developments.

“For about nine years, alongside various Communities of the Daughters of Saint Anne scattered throughout the world, groups of laypeople and priests have arisen, eager to share in the spirituality of the Institute […]. There are even about ten priests and young aspirants to the priesthood who would like to shape their priestly lives according to our spirituality. This emerging richness and variety of life, one might say spontaneous, alongside our communities in the various continents, was carefully considered during the Chapter and the subject of humble prayer.” (NEW LIFE, Acts of the 18th General Chapter, 1991. Congregation of the Daughters of Saint Anne).

Therefore, during the 18th General Chapter of the Daughters of Saint Anne, held in Rome from December 3 to January 28, 1991, the Chapter members approved the request, repeatedly presented by several aspirants, to be aggregated in various canonical forms to the Institute of the Daughters of Saint Anne.

This “New Life”, nurtured within the Family of the Daughters of Saint Anne, reveals to the Church and to History the richness and fruitfulness of the gift God granted to Blessed Mother Anna Rosa Gattorno.

“In [distant] vision I saw many great things for our Institute; a light allowed me to see the great panorama of the Order in the future. I must say that the divine [project] was so beautiful and intricate that I was ecstatic and delighted while I saw in it a river of numerous sufferings...” (Memorie, p. 320)

Despite her zealous concern, the projects undertaken in her time took other forms, for which the Mother herself repeatedly wondered whether they were in accordance with the will of God. In her Memorie, she writes, with regret, on the matter:

“The work of the tertiaries, and moreover arranged with the Bishop? This will not be it, but rather some other [thing] for which one will have to struggle...” (Memorie, p. 664)

“The uninitiated work of the Sons of Saint Anne gives me great sorrow, because I see that it is not as God desires it… […] I see and feel that Jesus does not find His delight...” (Memorie, p. 853)

Sustained by the certainty that, at the proper time, God’s hour would arrive, Mother Rosa entrusted the realization of these singular plans to Divine Providence. The Institute of the Daughters of Saint Anne would, at various other moments in history, seek to give life to her inspirations, seeking other juridical forms more in harmony with the times. But, as with every plan of God, His hour must be awaited.

For this reason, we believe that in 1991, for the entire Family of Saint Anne, the long-awaited hour of God finally seemed to have arrived for Mother Rosa. It is the Institute of the Daughters of Saint Anne itself, docile to God’s will and attentive to the signs of the times, which, after hearing from various authoritative persons, gave form and continuity to the different inspirations that the Mother had received from her Beloved Crucified:

“The Chapter members unanimously felt inspired to accept their repeatedly expressed request to be aggregated or associated in a precise canonical form with the Institute of the Daughters of Saint Anne. Therefore, it was unanimously decided to add to the 3rd article of the Constitutions the following statement: ‘By virtue of this spirit, the Family of the Daughters of Saint Anne is open to receiving other forms of evangelical life that are inspired by the same charism’.” (NEW LIFE, Acts of the 18th General Chapter, 1991. Congregation of the Daughters of Saint Anne).

In this regard, the Chapter approved inserting a new chapter into the Constitutions, with the following formulation:

“AGGREGATIONS AND ASSOCIATIONS. Open to the universal breath of the Spirit, which incessantly raises up new forms of life wherever, whenever, and however He wills, the Congregation of the Daughters of Saint Anne is ready to welcome those forms of evangelical life in which it recognizes the imprint of its Charism and which, as such, are confirmed by the authority of the Church. And, constantly striving toward the greater good of brothers and the extension of the Kingdom, it gives thanks to the Father for every gift.” (Constitutions of the Sisters, Daughters of Saint Anne, art. 191).

This is the living and concrete testimony that the Daughters of Saint Anne, “open to the universal breath of the Spirit”, hand down to the entire Charismatic Family, which, in this new time, consolidates Mother Rosa’s “dream”, confident that their docility will help God’s will continue to be fulfilled in and through them.

“Around every Religious Family, as well as around Societies of Apostolic Life and Secular Institutes, there exists a larger family, the ‘Charismatic Family,’ which includes several Institutes that recognize the same Charism, and above all lay Christians who feel called, each in their own condition, to share in the same charismatic reality.” (Pope Francis, on the occasion of the Year of Consecrated Life, III-1).

In light of what Pope Francis has written, we too are growing in awareness that no Charism is self-sufficient. Every Charism, entrusted to the hands of a founder or foundress, is destined for the entire People of God and, only if welcomed and lived by the various members of the People of God, can it fully unleash its potential.

Along this path, for over 40 years, the Charismatic Family of Saint Anne, founded by Blessed Anna Rosa Gattorno, can be considered a fruitful reality within the Church: the Religious Institute of the Daughters of Saint Anne, the Contemplative Perpetual Adorers Daughters of Saint Anne, the Religious Institute of the Sons of Saint Anne, the Secular Institute of the Daughters of Saint Anne, and the Movement of Hope.

“In faithful response to a common charismatic call, and conscious of being members of the same family, forge bonds of friendship in fraternal charity and nurture the hope of reaching the same ideal.”

(Cfr. Documents of base, p. 11).

The Charismatic Family of Saint Anne is made up of different Institutes and a Movement — people of various states of life: laypeople, religious sisters and brothers, priests, and secular members — who recognize themselves as belonging to the same Charism of Mother Rosa. Through her, we are united with one another in the fraternity of Christ, a supernatural climate realized in our common identification with Him and, in Him, with our brothers and sisters, and manifested in a communion of prayer and life (cfr. Documents of base, p. 12).
